scene.note: Instead of looking again after a timer, the price list hands the docket what to do when the count arrives.

steps.note: The price list calls then() on the card docket, which is still pending, with one callback for a count and one for a failure.
then() cannot run anything yet, so it keeps the callbacks on the docket and returns.
When the file has been read, resolve settles the docket, the one moment that knows the count is there.
The callback for that outcome runs once with the count, and the other one does not run at all.
The posters were counted by hand, so their docket is kept before then() is called.
Nothing will settle that docket again, so then() looks at its state itself.
The outcome is already known, so the matching callback runs with the docket's value.
The price list reads the card count twice, so two callbacks wait on one docket, in the order they were added.
When the docket is kept, every waiting callback gets its turn, first added first.
A then() with no callback for failures has nothing to run when a count fails, and that is skipped quietly.
